rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Measles is a highly contagious notifiable viral disease in England and Wales.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Suspected cases should be notified promptly to the local health protection team for risk assessment and public-health action.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: National guidance covers case details, laboratory investigation, infectious periods, contact assessment and outbreak management.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Two appropriately timed doses of measles-containing vaccine provide the main population-level prevention measure.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: People with measles should avoid contact with others during the infectious period specified in national guidance.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Close-contact management prioritises people at increased risk of severe disease and settings where transmission consequences are high.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Travel-associated cases require coordinated contact tracing and international notification arrangements.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA surveillance and vaccination-coverage monitoring support detection and control of measles transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Measles risk depends on vaccination, immunity, contact intensity, setting, travel, infectious timing, age and host vulnerability.

rows.source: UKHSA measles case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA measles evidence is case-, contact-, vaccine-, setting-, travel- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Rubella spreads through direct contact or respiratory droplets and is monitored through national surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Rubella infection can have serious consequences during pregnancy because of risk to the unborn baby.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance covers symptoms, diagnosis, management, surveillance, epidemiology and vaccination.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Immunisation is the principal prevention measure against rubella.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: The routine childhood programme uses two doses of a rubella-containing combined vaccine.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: From January 2026 the routine programme offers MMRV at 12 and 18 months for eligible children.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Vaccination coverage data are used to assess population protection and elimination progress.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Suspected or confirmed cases require public-health assessment with particular attention to pregnancy-related exposure.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: Rubella risk depends on immunity, vaccination, pregnancy, contact intensity, setting, laboratory confirmation and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA rubella surveillance and immunisation guidance
rows.verified: UKHSA rubella evidence is case-, contact-, pregnancy-, vaccine-, surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
